title: Quantum Simulation of the Static Yukawa Model via Effective Particles on a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulator
authors: Qingfeng Wang, Christopher G. Yale, Edward C. Tortorici, Brian K. McFarland, Daniel Lobser, Melissa C. Revelle, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, Peter J. Love
abstract: Trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and circuit QED quantum computers naturally enable coupled qubit-boson simulations. Boson-fermion interactions arise in quantum field theory, where renormalization is required to obtain finite results. We study one of the simplest examples of a coupled fermion-boson system, the static Yukawa model, on the QSCOUT trapped-ion system. We use similarity renormalization to express the same physics in terms of effective particles described by different values of the renormalization parameter $s$. This enables us to map data taken in the window of bosonic occupancy that is experimentally accessible to larger occupancies of distinct effective particles. We use this to study strongly coupled, high-occupancy regimes despite limited readout ranges. Using a trapped-ion qubit-boson device on Sandia National Laboratories' QSCOUT platform, we demonstrate the time evolution of the static Yukawa model.
summary: The authors demonstrate a method to simulate the static Yukawa model, a coupled fermion-boson system, on a trapped-ion quantum computer. They overcome the limitation of low bosonic occupancy readout by using a Renormalization Group procedure to map the physics onto effective particles. This allows for the study of strongly coupled, high-occupancy regimes previously unreachable by direct measurement.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of simulating strongly coupled fermion-boson systems, specifically the static Yukawa model, in regimes of high bosonic occupancy that are experimentally inaccessible due to current quantum simulator readout limitations.
main_result: By employing the Renormalization Group Procedure for Effective Particles (RGPEP), the authors successfully map the physics of high-occupancy regimes onto measurable low-occupancy measurements on a trapped-ion quantum simulator.
method: The core methodology involves using similarity renormalization transformations to define effective Hamiltonians ($H_s$) that allow the time evolution of the system to be simulated by measuring observables related to the bare Hamiltonian ($H$) in the experimentally accessible parameter space.
model_or_system: The system is the static Yukawa model, a coupled fermion-boson system, simulated on the QSCOUT trapped-ion quantum simulator. The dynamics are governed by Hamiltonians involving bosonic and fermionic operators, and the simulation utilizes qubit-boson interactions.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical problem and the RGPEP framework, detailing the Hamiltonian transformation. It then describes the experimental implementation on the trapped-ion platform, focusing on the measurement protocols (AJC interaction, fitting $P_{|1angle}(	heta)$). Finally, it presents the theoretical derivations and experimental results demonstrating the recovery of high-occupancy physics.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of quantum simulation by providing a systematic theoretical and experimental pathway to overcome hardware limitations (readout range) when simulating complex, strongly interacting many-body physics.
